lead: >-
  This 10-day journey connects Santiago, Valparaíso, Rapa Nui archaeological sites and the Maipo wine valley. The focus is on several different Easter Island excursions, not a brief stop to see moai. Discover the distribution of days, differences between private and group sections, flights and expenses to budget for separately.
---

## Chile and Easter Island in 10 days: how much time is spent on Rapa Nui?

**This ten-day itinerary suits travellers who want to spend several substantial days on [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/) and combine it with mainland Chile.** The journey includes 9 nights, starting and ending in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). Before the island section, there is a sightseeing excursion in the capital and a trip to the Pacific coast. After returning from Rapa Nui, a separate day is devoted to the [Maipo](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) wine region.

Rapa Nui culture is the main theme of the itinerary. Moai sculptures are fascinating in themselves, but three days of island excursions let you explore connected places: the quarry, platforms with erected statues, a ceremonial village and sites illustrating different periods of the island's history. The order of these visits is what distinguishes the tour from a short trip with only a few stops.

It is useful to compare this ten-day itinerary with [Colourful Santiago and Mysterious Easter Island, a six-day journey](/chile/tour/santiago-easter-island/). The shorter version groups the island excursions more tightly. Here there is more time for different areas of Rapa Nui and a separate day for Chilean wine tasting. If you also want the Atacama Desert and Patagonia, consider the [12-day Chile itinerary](/chile/tour/best-of-chile-easter-island-12-days/).

## Days 1–3: Santiago, port cities and a first introduction to Chile

The journey begins with an airport welcome in Santiago and a transfer to the hotel. The next day features a private sightseeing tour of the capital. In the city centre are La Moneda Palace and historic squares, while modern districts against the Andes reveal another side of Santiago. It is a convenient introduction after a long flight without immediately heading to a remote region.

On day 3, the route leads to the ocean, visiting [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/). Along the way, you pass vineyards, orchards and agricultural areas of the Curacaví and Casablanca valleys. Valparaíso is known for steep hills, old port architecture and urban lifts. Viña del Mar presents a more resort-oriented side of the coast. The two cities are convenient to visit together, but this is not a full beach holiday: the day is devoted to excursions and travel.

**Guiding arrangements differ by section:** the private Santiago city tour is included separately, while excursions outside the capital and on the island are conducted in groups. If you require a private guide on every day, those arrangements must be agreed explicitly; the word 'private' in the tour's name does not apply automatically to the entire itinerary.

## Why several days are devoted to Easter Island excursions

Day 4 includes a flight from Santiago to Easter Island and a hotel transfer. The island is remote from mainland Chile, with a different natural and cultural setting. [Hanga Roa](/chile/place/hanga-roa/) is its main settlement, while archaeological sites are spread across the island. Check-in, baggage collection and transfer time should therefore not be counted as a full excursion day.

Day 5 features a route to [Anakena](/chile/place/anakena-beach/) and major archaeological sites. The best-known include [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) and [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/). Rano Raraku shows how moai were carved from volcanic tuff: statues survive at different stages of production and transport. Ahu Tongariki demonstrates how the stone figures were arranged on ceremonial platforms. The history of these structures is far more complex than the familiar image of isolated stone figures standing in a field.

On day 6, attention shifts to [Orongo](/chile/place/orongo-village/) and [Rano Kau Volcano](/chile/place/rano-kau-volcano/). Orongo is associated with ceremonial traditions that developed after the era of monumental moai construction. Its surviving stone buildings and rock carvings provide historical context. The route towards the crater also offers natural panoramas of the island.

Day 7 includes [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) with its seven moai and [Puna Pau Quarry](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/), where the reddish stone for some statues' headdresses was extracted. These sites help explain the technology and symbolism of the monuments. Visiting different parts of the island makes the changing landscapes and position of the platforms easier to appreciate.

Archaeological areas are protected. Visitors must follow local guides' instructions and access rules. Monuments may be photographed from authorised paths, but crossing barriers or touching the statues is prohibited.

## Day 9: why the Maipo wine valley completes the trip

Day 8 brings a return flight to Santiago. After time on the remote island, it makes sense to leave room to rest before the final excursion. The following day takes place in the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) and introduces local winemaking with a tasting of Chilean wines.

Maipo contrasts with coastal Valparaíso and Rapa Nui's archaeological sites: the focus is on central Chile's agricultural culture, vineyards and the characteristics of different wine varieties. This finale suits adult travellers who want a relaxed gastronomic excursion after days devoted to history. For underage participants, tasting alcoholic drinks is not a compulsory service; an alternative format must be agreed.

Day 10 is reserved for the airport transfer. The journey therefore combines the capital and coast, several thematic days on the island and a winery excursion, with a break between flights.

## Flights, hotels and expenses: what to confirm before booking

The base programme includes accommodation in hotels of the chosen category with breakfast, meals where specified, transfers and excursions according to the itinerary. The private Santiago city tour is listed separately, while island excursions and journeys outside the capital take place in groups.

**Flights are not included.** This is a significant condition: in addition to international tickets, travellers need Santiago–Easter Island–Santiago flights. Their prices and seat availability affect whether the trip can take place on the desired dates. Tips, early check-in and late check-out at hotels are also separate expenses.

Do not confuse the 9 nights of the entire programme with an arbitrary number of island nights. The itinerary has mainland stops before and after the island, and the flight back from Rapa Nui is scheduled for day 8. Changes to flights may require rearranging the entire sequence, especially when adding extra island days.

| Part of the itinerary | Days |
|---|---|
| Santiago and the coast | 1–3 |
| Rapa Nui and its monuments | 4–7 |
| Return and Maipo | 8–10 |

Before buying flights, confirm current rules for entering the island, accommodation documentation and national park access with Chilean and local authorities. Conditions can change; descriptions of attractions do not replace the required documents for a specific arrival.

## Who is this ten-day itinerary for?

It is a good choice for people interested in archaeology and Polynesian history who want to combine Easter Island with several sides of mainland Chile. If your priorities are moai and convenient flights, compare the [shorter six-day itinerary](/chile/tour/santiago-easter-island/). For deserts, geysers and Patagonia, choose the [broader 12-day tour](/chile/tour/best-of-chile-easter-island-12-days/).

If you are selecting a destination rather than one specific ready-made itinerary, start with the [Chile tours catalogue](/chile/tour/) and our [Culture and History](/interests/culture-and-history/) collection.

## Frequently asked questions about the private Easter Island tour

### Are all excursions private?

No. The Santiago city tour is private; island excursions and outings outside the capital are conducted in groups. A different guiding format must be agreed separately.

### How many days are spent on Easter Island?

The flight to the island is scheduled for day 4, archaeological visits take place on days 5–7, and the return to Santiago is on day 8. That provides three main excursion days on Rapa Nui.

### Are domestic air tickets included?

No. Flights appear among the exclusions. In particular, the return flights to Easter Island must be factored into the budget.

### Can Patagonia be added to the itinerary?

Patagonia is not part of this ten-day route. You can consider a different programme, such as [Best of Chile](/chile/tour/best-of-chile-easter-island-12-days/), or discuss a customised extension of the trip.

### What makes the Maipo day worthwhile?

It is devoted to central Chile's wine region and a tasting of local wines. This is a separate gastronomic theme after the archaeological excursions, not another day on Easter Island.

## VIP Chile 5*: Santiago, Atacama and Patagonia in 10 days

This [10-day premium Chile tour](/chile/tour/chile-five-star-vip/) brings together three very different geographical regions. The first days take place in Santiago and the Maipo wine valley. The programme then moves north to Atacama's red rocks, salt flats and geysers, before heading to southern Patagonia and Grey Glacier. Day 9 is devoted to the Pacific coast of [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/).

Unlike a holiday within one region, this journey involves numerous flights. The key considerations are **the exact number of nights, the chosen accommodation rate and the cost of domestic flights**.

## First days: Santiago and wine in the Maipo Valley

After arrival, there is a transfer to the hotel and free time. Day 2 includes a sightseeing excursion in Santiago followed by wine tasting in the Maipo Valley. In the evening, travellers can choose a restaurant to discover contemporary Chilean cuisine.

Accommodation options include The Singular Santiago. Exploring the capital provides a gradual transition from a long international flight to the demanding nature-focused portion of the itinerary.

## Atacama: Moon Valley, lagoons and geysers

Day 3 involves a flight to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This is the departure point for desert and high-altitude excursions.

Atacama's highlights include [Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/), the salt flat and lagoons. On day 4, travellers visit [Miscanti](/chile/place/laguna-miscanti/) and [Miñiques](/chile/place/laguna-miniques/), discover the [Atacama Salt Flat](/chile/place/atacama-salt-flat/) and observe flamingos in the Chaxa area. Entrance tickets and lunch are included in the day's programme.

Day 5 starts early at the [El Tatio Geysers](/chile/place/el-tatio-geysers/), followed by a stop in Machuca village and a return to Santiago. The altitude, cold mornings and long distances require suitable clothing and readiness for full excursion days.

Accommodation in Atacama is at Nayara Alto Atacama. When comparing prices, distinguish lodging and included excursions from **the air tickets excluded from this package's base rate**.

## Patagonia and Grey Glacier

Day 6 includes a flight south to Puerto Natales, and day 7 a visit to [Torres del Paine National Park](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). A boat excursion to Grey Glacier, lakes, viewpoints and [Mylodon Cave](/chile/place/mylodon-cave/) are planned.

The park is known for granite peaks, glacial valleys and changeable weather. Navigating on the water and accessing particular natural sights depends on conditions. The programme includes sightseeing excursions, but a visit to Torres del Paine does not imply a multi-day W or O trek.

Accommodation options include The Singular Patagonia. On day 8, the group returns to Santiago, and day 9 is dedicated to [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/) before the journey ends.

## Accommodation and 2027 prices

The trip lasts **10 days / 9 nights**, with several per-person prices in US dollars. The rate depends on the number of guests and room occupancy.

| Group and room | USD/person |
|---|---:|
| 1 traveller, SGL | 22 347 |
| 2 travellers, SGL | 17 800 |
| 2 travellers, DBL | 11 785 |
| 3 travellers, SGL | 16 558 |
| 3 travellers, DBL | 10 542 |
| 3 travellers, TRP | 9 998 |

Accommodation options include The Singular Santiago, Nayara Alto Atacama and The Singular Patagonia, at 5-star standard or similar hotels subject to the terms. Breakfasts, specified meals, transfers, national park entrance tickets, excursions with transport and emergency support are included.

**International and domestic flights are not included in the prices above.** The exclusions list gives a domestic flight cost starting at USD 550. Insurance, meals outside the programme, discretionary tips, bank charges and a 5% fee for payment by card are also excluded.

## How it differs from a shorter gastronomy tour

The [7-day VIP Chile gastronomy tour](/chile/tour/chile-vip-atacama-patagonia-gourmet/) also combines Atacama and Patagonia, but moves more quickly and concentrates on culinary experiences on selected days. The 10-day programme adds the Maipo wine valley and a full excursion to the Pacific coast before departure.

If a gentler flight schedule and more days to discover the country matter to you, compare the exact overnight sequence of the two options rather than only the category names of their accommodation.

## Frequently asked questions about VIP Chile

### Are domestic flights included?

No. Domestic flights are charged separately, starting at USD 550.

### How many nights are included?

Nine nights, divided between Santiago, Atacama and Patagonia.

### Is the price the same for every guest?

No. The table shows different rates for 1, 2 or 3 guests and SGL, DBL or TRP accommodation.

### Does the itinerary include the ocean coast?

Yes. Day 9 is dedicated to a sightseeing trip to Valparaíso and Viña del Mar.

## Chile in 9 days: three distinct natural regions on one journey

The Hidden Treasures of Chile itinerary suits travellers interested in contrasts: northern salt flats and geothermal fields, icebergs in Patagonia, turquoise lakes and granite mountains in the far south. Over **9 days and 8 nights**, the journey includes road travel and flights between distant regions. This is an intensive sightseeing tour with excursion days, not a multi-day trek.

The first stage begins in [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). You then head to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The second part takes in [General Carrera Lake](/chile/place/general-carrera-lake/), San Rafael Glacier and [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). Several travel days connect these regions, so there is less free time than on a trip devoted to one area.

## What to see in Atacama and why spend three days there?

Atacama occupies days 2–4. After flying via Calama, there is a sunset excursion to [Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/). The next day features the high-altitude Miscanti and Miñiques lagoons, Socaire village, the [Atacama Salt Flat](/chile/place/atacama-salt-flat/) and Chaxa Lagoon in [Los Flamencos Reserve](/chile/place/los-flamencos-national-reserve/). The principal attractions are unusual landscapes and opportunities to see birds, including flamingos, without guaranteeing encounters.

Day 4 begins with an early departure to the [El Tatio Geysers](/chile/place/el-tatio-geysers/) and a stop in Machuca, followed by a return to Calama and a flight to Santiago. El Tatio is above 4,300 metres: even those in good physical shape should prepare for the cold at dawn and the effects of altitude. Warm clothes, water and care during rapid ascent are important.

Compare this section with other [Chile itineraries](/chile/tour/) if the desert is your principal reason for travelling and you are happy to leave Patagonia for another trip.

## Aysén: two water experiences that are easy to confuse

On day 5, you fly to Balmaceda and travel along the [Carretera Austral](/chile/place/carretera-austral/) to [Puerto Río Tranquilo](/chile/place/puerto-rio-tranquilo/). The route then includes **two different boat excursions**.

On day 6, a journey through Exploradores Valley and Bay takes you to [San Rafael Glacier](/chile/place/san-rafael-glacier/) and drifting icebergs. The objective is viewing the glacier from the water. Walking on the ice is not part of this programme; boat access depends on weather and navigation conditions.

On the morning of day 7, a private boat visits the [Marble Caves](/chile/place/marble-caves/) on General Carrera Lake. Natural arches and chambers have been shaped by water eroding the rock. Light, lake conditions and a safe passage by boat influence photography, so a particular image cannot be guaranteed at a set time.

If these two attractions are your main priority, see the separate [3-day Aysén itinerary](/chile/tour/marble-caves-san-rafael-3-days/). Without Atacama or Torres del Paine, it focuses on this one part of Patagonia.

## Torres del Paine and the main logistical challenge

After the Marble Caves on day 7, the itinerary includes a drive to Balmaceda Airport, a regional flight to Punta Arenas and a transfer to Puerto Natales. This connection is sensitive to flight schedules. The regional flight is planned with DAP Airlines; routes depend on weekdays and season, so **the dates of the entire nine-day journey are coordinated with the regional flight that is actually available**.

Day 8 features a group excursion to Mylodon Cave and [Torres del Paine National Park](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). Grey Lake, Pehoé, Salto Grande Waterfall and other scenic stops are listed. This is a sightseeing drive with nature stops, not a W Trek or an ascent towards the base of the granite towers.

Patagonian weather can change quickly. A rainproof windbreaker, warm layers and closed shoes will be useful even after Atacama's hot, dry days. Confirm luggage allowances for flights with a smaller regional carrier in advance: a large suitcase or hiking equipment may require different arrangements.

## Who the itinerary suits and what to verify in the offer

This route suits travellers comfortable with early departures, several flights and group excursions. It is particularly appealing to those who want to see the natural regions of northern and southern Chile in one trip. If you want a long hike in [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) or several restful days without travel, choose a different format.

We offer a rate for two travellers sharing a double room. Accommodation, agreed meals, excursions and entrance tickets are itemised separately. **There is an important detail regarding flights:** the general exclusions list air tickets as not included, but the description of day 4 expressly says the Calama–Santiago flight is included. When preparing the quote, Ada Tours confirms exactly which domestic flights are covered by the final price. Medical and travel insurance are not included in the source package.

## Frequently asked questions about the nine-day Chile tour

### Can you see Atacama and Patagonia without separate holidays?

Yes. This route links Chile's north and south by air, but the trade-off for saving calendar days is frequent travel. A more relaxed discovery of either region calls for a separate trip.

### Is the W Trek in Torres del Paine included?

No. The itinerary features a one-day sightseeing excursion in the park and Mylodon Cave. A multi-day W Trek is not part of the programme.

### Do you need to know how to steer a boat at the Marble Caves?

No. An organised boat excursion is planned, not self-driving a vessel. There is also an organised boat excursion on the San Rafael Glacier day.

### When should flights be agreed?

Before fixing dates and making payment. The Balmaceda–Punta Arenas leg is particularly important: its regional schedule affects the sequence of the entire trip. Luggage restrictions and which air tickets have been paid for should be confirmed at the same time.

## Chile in 6 days: ocean, Atacama and the starry sky

The name An Otherworldly Journey on Earth is explained by the scenery itself: the rocky ridges of [Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/), dry valleys, salt flats and volcanic highlands. Yet the programme covers more than the desert. It starts in the capital, includes a trip to the Pacific Ocean and only then takes travellers into Atacama.

The journey lasts **6 days and 5 nights**. It is a convenient format for a first introduction to the contrasts of central and northern Chile, provided you are prepared for early departures and frequent changes of scenery. It does not include Patagonia: if [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) is a priority, consider a separate [7-day itinerary through southern Chile](/chile/tour/chile-santiago-atacama-torres-del-paine/).

## Santiago and the coast: two different city experiences

Day 1 is devoted to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). Following an airport welcome and private transfer, there is an approximately four-hour sightseeing tour with a Russian-speaking guide. This matters for travellers who require Russian-language guiding: the group excursions to the coast and northern Chile use English-speaking guides.

Day 2 features [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/). Valparaíso attracts visitors with hillside neighbourhoods, stairways and colourful façades; Viña del Mar represents a more resort-oriented coastline. The excursion takes approximately 8–9 hours, making this a full sightseeing day rather than a short stop by the sea. Lunch in a fish restaurant can be purchased separately.

This opening lets travellers experience both urban Chile and the Pacific coast before the dry northern part of the country. Those already familiar with Santiago may find the following days the main reason to choose this trip.

## Atacama: rocky valleys, lagoons and flamingos

After a flight north, the route passes through [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The same day includes [Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/) and [Death Valley](/chile/place/death-valley-atacama/), where the shape of rocks and sandy slopes formed by wind and long geological processes is particularly visible. Sunset in Moon Valley is one of the main moments of the programme; the exact visit depends on the schedule and site access.

The next excursion day features the high-altitude [Miscanti Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-miscanti/) and Miñiques, the Atacama Salt Flat and [Chaxa Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-chaxa/). The region offers high-altitude scenery and opportunities to observe flamingos. These are natural sightings depending on season and bird behaviour, not a guaranteed performance.

An important detail: some outings reach approximately 4,300 metres. Even on a sightseeing trip rather than an athletic expedition, altitude, dry air and temperature differences matter. Prepare water, warm clothing and suitable shoes in advance.

## Stargazing: what is actually included?

Atacama is known for clear skies and excellent conditions for astronomy. After the valley excursions, this programme offers **an optional night-time astronomy excursion** with an English-speaking guide and telescopes. It costs an additional **$100 per person**. It is not automatically part of the standard package.

Read about our [standalone Atacama astronomy excursion](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/chile-atacama-astronomy-tour/) to distinguish it from daytime nature trips. Whether the observation can take place and which celestial objects are visible depends on weather, the Moon's phase and the actual visiting time. Telescope stargazing on every night cannot be guaranteed.

## Early El Tatio departure and return to Santiago

Day 5 begins very early: departure is around 05:00 for the [El Tatio Geysers](/chile/place/el-tatio-geysers/), with a visit to Machuca village. The geysers lie above 4,300 metres, and the cold at dawn makes the steam especially prominent. Afterwards, there is a transfer to the airport, a flight to Santiago and an overnight stay in the capital.

This is the most demanding day in the schedule: waking before dawn, altitude, a long transfer and a flight. Anyone who finds early starts difficult should evaluate the schedule before booking. The final sixth day is reserved for breakfast and an airport transfer.

## What's included and how to compare with other itineraries

We offer **4-star hotel accommodation** with breakfast, private transfers, a Russian-speaking guide for the Santiago sightseeing tour, group excursions with English-speaking guides on other days and entrance tickets along the route. Meals expressly specified in the programme are also included.

**International and domestic flights are paid for separately.** Medical insurance, optional excursions, food outside the programme and personal expenses are also excluded from the package price. Private outings with Russian-speaking guidance are described as a paid option rather than part of the base rate.

When choosing, compare two different scenarios:

| Tour | Main distinction |
|---|---|
| This six-day journey | Ocean, Valparaíso, Atacama |
| [North and Patagonia, 7 days](/chile/tour/chile-santiago-atacama-torres-del-paine/) | Lagoons, geysers and Torres del Paine |

The six-day route is more suitable for someone who wants to discover coastal cities and northern Chile. The seven-day option suits someone willing to skip the coast for an introduction to Patagonia. More options are available in our [Chile tours catalogue](/chile/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about An Otherworldly Journey on Earth

### Is the night-time astronomy excursion included in the price?

No. It is an optional excursion with a specified price of $100 per person. It must be arranged according to weather and observing conditions.

### Will there be a Russian-speaking guide on every excursion?

The standard programme specifies Russian-speaking guiding for the Santiago sightseeing tour. The coastal trip and Atacama excursions are planned with English-speaking guides; private Russian-language guiding is available for an extra charge.

### How physically demanding is this tour?

There is no sporting trek, but some excursions take place at high altitude and the geyser trip starts early in the morning. Consider your tolerance for altitude and a full schedule.

### Are Santiago–northern Chile flights included?

No. Domestic air tickets, like international flights, are listed among costs outside the package price.

## Chile in 7 days: Atacama and Torres del Paine

This seven-day route suits travellers who want to discover **two fundamentally different natural regions of Chile on one journey**. In Atacama, these include a salt flat, rocky valleys, high-altitude lagoons and geysers; in Patagonia, glacial lakes, granite peaks and waterfalls. Flights between the regions and a stop in Santiago are planned. It is an intensive week of sightseeing, not a leisurely holiday in one hotel.

Unlike the [6-day trip through Santiago, the coast and Atacama](/chile/tour/chile-otherworldly-journey/), this journey has no sightseeing day in Valparaíso but does include [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). The Patagonia section is the defining difference between the itineraries.

## Combining the northern desert and southern Patagonia

The journey begins in [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), visiting the historic centre, Plaza de Armas and the La Moneda Palace area. A flight to Calama then leads to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), a base for desert excursions. Allow time for the airport transfer: [Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/) is already scheduled for day 2.

The following days focus on high-altitude natural attractions. One excursion combines [Miscanti Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-miscanti/), Miñiques, [Chaxa Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-chaxa/) and Toconao village. The scenery includes both salt flats and volcanic landscapes. Flamingos can be seen in their natural habitat, but an encounter with a particular bird cannot be guaranteed.

A separate early outing visits the [El Tatio Geysers](/chile/place/el-tatio-geysers/) and Machuca village. The geyser field is above 4,300 metres, and clouds of steam are particularly impressive at sunrise in the cold air. Warm layers, water and attention to how you feel at altitude are essential. This is one of the days when the early departure time has a major impact on rest.

The southern portion begins with travel to Puerto Natales. The sightseeing day includes [Mylodon Cave](/chile/place/mylodon-cave/), panoramas of Grey Lake, Salto Grande and other viewpoints in the national park. The landscape changes from wooded areas to exposed, windy lakeshores and mountain ranges.

## How physically demanding is the journey?

The programme includes transport, scenic stops and walks, including to the shore of Grey Lake and in the Salto Grande area. **There is no multi-day W Trek or ascent to the base of the Torres towers on this itinerary.** It would therefore be misleading to assess its difficulty by the standards of athletic treks in Patagonia.

Two aspects need attention. Some Atacama excursions take place at high altitude, while weather in Patagonia can change quickly, bringing wind and rain. Clothing for a sunny or hot desert day will not replace windproof and waterproof layers for the south. Comfortable shoes, a hat and sunscreen are useful.

The national park has established access regulations. Torres del Paine and Mylodon Cave entrance tickets are already included in the tour price. Independent travellers comparing formats should note that entry tickets and access to specific areas of the park are governed by current park administration rules.

## Flights and the full itinerary

The route connects at least two distant regions by air: Santiago–Calama and southern Patagonia, with a return to the capital. Connections and intermediate transfers between the northern excursions and Puerto Natales must be arranged according to the actual flight tickets. **International and domestic flights are not included** in the tour price.

The schedule is particularly full around the early El Tatio excursion, road transfers and the next change of region. When selecting flights, use the actual day-by-day itinerary rather than just the headline duration of '7 days': some calendar days are occupied by travel.

The tour includes accommodation with breakfasts, the specified excursions and group guiding services, planned transfers, meals and admission tickets according to the programme. Air tickets, insurance, some meals and personal expenses are paid separately. Check tipping arrangements and bank fees before deciding how to pay.

## Who this tour is for

This journey is primarily for travellers interested in [Chile's natural landscapes](/interests/wildlife/tours/chile/), the contrast between desert and Patagonia and varied scenery during a limited holiday. Santiago offers a brief city introduction, while most of the time is devoted to nature excursions.

If Pacific beaches, colourful port cities or a dedicated evening astronomy excursion are your main priorities, compare this itinerary with [An Otherworldly Journey on Earth](/chile/tour/chile-otherworldly-journey/). If you want a major hike through Torres del Paine, choose a programme that specifically includes the trekking route.

## Frequently asked questions about the Atacama and Torres del Paine tour

### Can you properly see northern and southern Chile in 7 days?

The route visits key places in both regions in an intensive sightseeing format. There is little time to explore each independently at a relaxed pace, because some days involve flights and transfers.

### Is the hike to the Torres del Paine towers included?

No. The programme includes a vehicle-based national park tour, viewpoints and short walks near lakes and the waterfall, not the route to the base of the granite towers.

### When is preparation for cold weather especially important?

On the early-morning El Tatio geyser day and when visiting windy Patagonia. These sections require different warm and protective layers, even if Santiago and lowland Atacama are warm.

### Are domestic flights paid for separately?

Yes. Air tickets are listed among services excluded from the package price. Confirm the route and connections for your chosen dates before finalising the trip.
